nodes.label: JEDI
nodes.description: Joint Energy Development Investments, L.P. — a $500 million Enron / CalPERS investment partnership (1993), kept off Enron's balance sheet because control was shared.

nodes.label: Chewco
nodes.description: Chewco Investments, L.P. — formed in 1997 to buy CalPERS' stake in JEDI. It never had the 3% independent equity the accounting rules required, so JEDI should have been consolidated: part of Enron's November 2001 restatement.

nodes.label: LJM1
nodes.description: LJM Cayman, L.P. — formed in June 1999, with the CFO as general partner, to 'hedge' Enron's investment in Rhythms NetConnections.

nodes.label: LJM2
nodes.description: LJM2 Co-Investment, L.P. — a larger CFO-managed private-equity fund (late 1999) that transacted with Enron and provided the outside equity of the Raptors.

nodes.label: Talon (Raptor I)
nodes.description: Raptor I's vehicle, funded mostly with Enron's own stock, used to offset losses on Enron's merchant investments (2000).

nodes.label: Timberwolf (Raptor II)
nodes.description: Raptor II's vehicle — the same Enron-stock-funded 'hedge' structure as Talon.

nodes.label: Porcupine (Raptor III)
nodes.description: Raptor III's vehicle, funded with Enron's holding in The New Power Company.

nodes.label: Bobcat (Raptor IV)
nodes.description: Raptor IV's vehicle — the last Raptor, set up in September 2000.

nodes.label: Southampton Place
nodes.description: Southampton Place, L.P. — a partnership through which the CFO's family foundation and several Enron employees invested in the unwinding of the Rhythms hedge (March 2000), with extraordinary returns.

nodes.label: Arthur Andersen
nodes.description: Enron's outside auditor, which also advised on the structure and accounting of the related-party transactions.

nodes.label: The Travel Agency in the Park
nodes.description: A travel agency (later Alliance Worldwide) that Enron employees paid for business travel — $362,096 on the insider-pay schedule.
